tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms/intent (agent won't start, gateway fails, returns nothing, behaves differently in prod, which version is live) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly covers trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name domain terms ('even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name'), and is concise (a short paragraph).
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious facts (AgentCore vs Classic distinctions, specific API calls, specific check-ids) rather than explaining generic concepts the agent already knows. It never pauses to explain what VPC endpoints or IAM are in general terms.
tests.evidence: Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under `references/`: `checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001..014...) and `checks-agents.md` (LLM-AGT-001..011...).

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (check catalogs, metrics, quirks) is consistently pushed to references/ files and only referenced by id/table row in the body; the router table links out instead of embedding details inline.
tests.evidence: Load it with any row. ... | AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | ... | `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001) |

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All 8 reference files are linked via markdown links somewhere in the body (collection-reference.md, checks-agentcore.md, checks-agents.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, related-skills.md, router-details.md, runtime-sessions.md).
tests.evidence: [`references/router-details.md`](references/router-details.md): the full first-read method for the longer Router rows.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: References are embedded in a router table keyed by trigger phrase ('Operator says') which conditions when to load each file, and other links specify triggering conditions (e.g., VPC endpoint checks, OTLP configs).
tests.evidence: | AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | `ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` for status, version, role ARN | `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001) |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<file>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, order-dependent operations (the two review procedures) are given exact ordered steps with checkboxes, while flexible analytical judgment areas (hypothesis labeling, scope disclosure) are described with rationale rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: Step 2: Simulate the runtime role with `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` for every action it exercises ... any required action `denied` is **LLM-AC-001 (CRITICAL)**.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple paths exist (e.g., migration options), a primary default is clearly recommended with an alternative noted briefly.
tests.evidence: recommend migrating via the **AgentCore harness** (config-based, closest analog) or **code-defined agents on AgentCore**

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach generalizable methods (resolve alias to version, simulate IAM policy, check gateway targets) applicable to any runtime/agent instance, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Read the runtime with `bedrock-agent:ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` — status, version, endpoint, and the execution **role ARN**

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus Error Handling with specific traps, which functions as a gotchas section with concrete, non-obvious corrections.
tests.evidence: "GetAgent shows PREPARED, so that config is what production runs." An agent's live behaviour is its **alias → version** resolution, not the latest prepared DRAFT.
